newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut hits high in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut hits high in Beirut.

text.p: Bank shares gained ground on the Beirut Stock Exchange and Bank of Beirut hit a record high of $5 on Friday.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.76 percent to 190.83. The BLOM general index fell 0.56 percent to 1,118.21 and the LISPI general index climbed 0.04 percent to 96.29 percent.
Bank of Beirut rose to $5 from $4.9375 -- a 130 percent rise over its issue price. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $22 from $21.875 and Banque Audi climbed to $28.6250 from $28.5.
"Bank shares did well for the end of the week," said a broker.
Solidere A shares held steady at $13.00 and B shares dropped to $13.2500 from $13.5.
"There was a little more supply than demand for Solidere but the supply was less than Thursday's level," said a broker.
BSE turnover fell to 232,788 from 388,834 for a value of $2,733,994 against $5,033,388.
There was no trade in the other three listed industrial firms -- Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
On Thursday, Lebanon's Allied Business Bank said it expected to launch the country's first mutual fund soon and was planning two other funds, all worth a total of $7 million.
Brokers said the move was good news for the Lebanese market but one bourse watcher said it did not have an impact on the BSE on Friday.
